scope: Standing 1907 square red-brick chimney of the Tai Tam Tuk Raw Water Pumping Station, with masonry stepped base, tapered shaft, oversailing coping, and the visible crown of the inclined brick flue.
geometryBasis: Hong Kong government heritage map feature 896 binds both the square uphill end and long descending flue. Original 5 m elevation samples register both parts of the structure on the slope.
sectionBasis: Tapered square brick chimney with offset plinth and oversailing upper coping. The measured survey height is 19.304 m; the flue follows the official narrow boundary toward the pumping station.
limitations: The heritage survey supplies the chimney height. The width fitted within the marked base, top width, stepped cornice details and the small inspection aperture are estimates.
Only the visible crown of the inclined flue and exposed base are represented. The exact exterior exposure of the brick conduit and its connection into the pumping station are approximate.
The original 5 m terrain is preserved. The ground can obscure individual brick steps and local foundation joints.

facts.flue: smoke tunnel connected to the engine hall
